title: ZenPath — Relevance under the hood (Hosted API tour)
summary: Hosted API demo focused on embedding + rerank flow, architecture tradeoffs, POC scope. Customer cares about p95 latency, recall for long-tail queries, SOC2/compliance, and cost. SE showed live console, API calls, and Optimize suggestions. Agreed next step: pilot with 100k doc subset and benchmark run; pricing & security pack to be shared.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 09:21 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (ZenPath Head of Search), Omar Hulse (ZenPath Platform Eng), Dana Lee (ZenPath Data Scientist), Alex Gomez (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, I'll hand off to Liam to walk through the embeddings + reranker flow in the hosted API. Quick who we have on the call?
[00:07] Priya: Hi, Priya here, head of search at ZenPath. We're trying to improve relevance across our enterprise docs and product QA.
[00:12] Omar: Omar — platform, I'll be implementing POC infra.
[00:15] Dana: Dana, DS working on ranking models.
[00:18] Alex: Alex, PM for the search product.
[00:20] Liam: Great thanks, quick agenda — architecture, demo in Console, live API call, rerank examples, then Q&A and POC next steps.
[00:30] Liam: So at a high level we recommend a two-stage retrieval: embeddings search to get ~100 candidates, then our reranker endpoint to score and reorder. This lets you balance recall and precision and keep p95 latencies predictable.
[00:45] Priya: Quick question — are you assuming a vector DB like Pinecone or do you host vectors in Redwood?
[00:52] Liam: Good call — hosted API provides embeddings only; you can store vectors wherever you want. Many customers use Pinecone/FAISS/Weaviate. For the POC we can also run a small in-memory recall check from our demo console just to show signals.
[01:05] Omar: Important for us — we have a 200ms p95 target in the UI, how realistic is that with reranking step?
[01:12] Liam: For 100 candidates reranked on a moderate model optimized for CPU/GPU we see end-to-end p95 from 120ms to 450ms depending on model choice and token lengths. With our suggested quantized reranker and prefix caching you'll be around 180-260ms. There's a tradeoff with quality.
[01:30] Maya: We'll show latency numbers live. Also note Optimize will give batching and cache suggestions based on your workload.
[01:40] Liam: Jumping into the Console — open the Hosted API -> Models -> Embeddings. You'll see model variants and size/throughput profiles. (screen share)
[02:05] Liam: Here I'm uploading a sample dataset of 12k support articles — for demo simplicity, but you said your dataset is ~100k docs?
[02:12] Priya: Yes, roughly 120k chunked docs after preprocessing.
[02:15] Liam: Good — for POC we'll target 100k subset. In Console I can run a quick embed call: POST /v1/embeddings {"model":"rw-embed-v1","input":"How to reset password"} — returns a 1536-dim vector. Raw latency here is ~45ms for the embedding call.
[02:40] Liam: Now we run a similarity search (demo uses local FAISS in the console) to pull top 100, show raw BM25 vs vector recall metrics. BM25 nails exact-match but misses paraphrase.
[03:05] Dana: Are your embeddings deterministic across runs? We need stable vectors for incremental updates.
[03:09] Liam: Embeddings are deterministic for the same model and quantization; if you switch model versions you'll see shifts. We recommend version pinning. Also we provide a vector migration plan in docs.
[03:20] Priya: Security — SOC2? data retention? SSO?
[03:24] Maya: Short answers: SOC2 Type II yes, we have SAML/SSO and RBAC. Data retention can be configured per-tenant; hosted API returns are ephemeral unless you choose to store logs. We'll send the security pack after the call.
[03:42] Liam: Back to reranker: The rerank endpoint accepts the query and candidate doc text or doc ids + cached embeddings. For performance we recommend sending embeddings for candidates (so the model doesn't recompute). Example request: POST /v1/rerank with {"query":"...","candidates":[{id,text,embedding},...]} — sending 100 embeddings is often fastest.
[04:05] Alex: That sounds like a lot of payload — any tips to keep request size manageable?
[04:10] Liam: Yes, use compact float16 embeddings and compression or store embeddings server-side and pass ids; then we can fetch them internally with an authenticated vector-store integration. The Console shows both workflows.
[04:25] [05:00] Liam: Ok quick live rerank demo, I'm sending top100 candidates, model rw-rerank-v1-q8 (quantized). p95 in this environment: 230ms, mean 150ms. Outputs include score and rationale tokens if you enable structured output.
[05:30] Priya: Rationale tokens — can we get highlight spans for UI?
[05:35] Liam: Yes, enable span_extraction and it returns candidate spans with offsets, though that increases runtime. Good for UX where you want snippet highlights.
[06:00] Omar: For throughput we might need to batch 10 concurrent UI calls, what's Redwood's approach?
[06:08] Liam: Use continuous batching and autoscale on Dedicated; hosted has autoscaling but you can configure concurrency limits and Optimize will suggest batch sizes to maximize tokens/second while meeting latency SLOs.
[06:25] Maya: I'll pivot to common POC success metrics — Priya you mentioned precision uplift and p95. Usually customers set: +10-15 MRR or commercial MRR? (small laugh)
[06:38] Priya: We want MRR? sorry— mean reciprocal rank improvement is our metric, MRR and click-through rate.
[06:45] Maya: Great — propose targets: MRR +0.12 (12% relative) on head queries, p95 < 250ms at 99% of sessions, and cost per 1k queries under $X.
[06:58] Dana: Cost — do you provide cost estimator for hosted?
[07:02] Liam: Yes, Console -> Optimize -> Cost estimator. It takes your queries per minute, candidate size, model selection, and suggests batching and quantization to hit a cost target. We can run your telemetry through Optimize in the pilot.
[07:20] Alex: Any hard limits on document size or tokenization?
[07:24] Liam: For embeddings we chunk at ~1k tokens recommended; reranker has a max input token budget — if you send full doc text you'll need truncation. Best practice: embed chunks and rerank chunk-level then aggregate. We provide aggregation helpers in our SDK.
[07:45] [08:15] Liam: Now quick demo of the quickstart notebook — (switches to notebook) — here is a simple Python snippet: from redwood import Client; c = Client(os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); v = c.embeddings.create(model='rw-embed-v1', input=batch_queries); then index into Pinecone and call rerank via c.rerank.score(...). I'll paste this into the chat.
[08:40] Priya: Could you also show how Optimize would change batching if query length distribution skewed to long queries?
[08:46] Liam: Sure — enable workload profiling, Optimize flags that long-tail queries reduce effective batch sizes and suggests switching to a smaller rerank model for long queries or enabling prefix caching if queries reuse prefixes.
[09:05] Dana: We're worried about QA/regression — how do we ensure reranker changes don't regress intents?
[09:11] Liam: We have evaluation harness: you can upload labeled query sets, run A/B in Console, and get quality delta metrics (MRR, recall@k, precision@k). Also automatic quality monitoring pushes alerts on regressions.
[09:30] Maya: Let's cover integration options — hosted API (fastest), Dedicated for predictable capacity and VPC peering, or Private for air-gapped. Which are you leaning to for POC?
[09:40] Priya: Likely Hosted for POC, but Dedicated mid-term if we keep latency guarantees and throughput.
[09:45] Omar: VPC peering would be nice; we have strict egress rules.
[09:49] Maya: Hosted supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys at rest; we'll include network diagrams in the follow-up.
[10:05] Alex: Any privacy issues — will content ever leave region or be used for model training?
[10:11] Liam: No training on customer data by default, and you can opt into usage-sharing. Data residency: we support regioned endpoints.
[10:20] [11:00] Liam: Wrapping demo — live benchmark we ran earlier against a 100k subset: baseline BM25 MRR 0.42, embeddings+rerank MRR 0.58, p95 240ms with quantized reranker. We'll reproduce this with your queries as part of pilot.
[11:25] Priya: Sounds promising. For the pilot we want to test 100k docs, 10k unique queries, 2-week window, measure MRR and UI latency.
[11:33] Maya: Agreed. I'll send a pilot statement of work and pricing options. Liam will run an initial benchmark and share the script.
[12:00] Omar: Who needs to be in the kickoff?
[12:05] Dana: DS + platform + 2 engineers for integration.
[12:10] Maya: Noted.
[12:15] [12:45] Q&A rapid fire:
[12:45] Priya: Does reranker support multi-document context?
[12:49] Liam: You can send multiple candidates; for cross-doc reasoning reranker is limited — we recommend retrieval-augmented generation flow for cross-document synthesis.
[13:10] Alex: Billing model for hosted rerank calls?
[13:14] Maya: Per-request tokens + per-embedding unit; pilot pricing is often flat with usage cap for two weeks.
[13:25] Priya: Any known failure modes?
[13:28] Liam: Long candidate lists without caching blow up latency; also switching models midstream can change embedding geometry and require reindexing.
[13:40] [14:10] Closing recap — Maya: action items and next steps. We'll send security pack, pilot SOW, quickstart notebook, and benchmark script. Schedule kickoff next Tue 2026-03-09.
[14:35] Priya: Thanks, excited to try it.
[14:38] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up shortly.
[14:45] Recording end.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlaps; some technical terms auto-corrected (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cake" in one spot).
